# Synthetic reviewer request and excerpt

This is my synthetic draft; I permit review in this environment. Please provide a focused qualitative-methods assessment in English, not a whole-paper editorial recommendation. Do not use external services. No journal specified.

Title: Making sense of professional transitions.
Field/design: qualitative psychology, contextualist reflexive thematic analysis.

## Methods — Recruitment and analysis
We purposively recruited 18 adults with varied transition experiences. Interviews lasted 55–80 minutes. We aimed for interpretive depth and variation, not population prevalence estimates. The first analyst kept reflexive memos on her own career experience. Both analysts discussed evolving interpretations; coding differences were resources for reflection rather than measurement error. We did not calculate inter-coder reliability or claim saturation. Theme development involved repeated engagement with transcripts, candidate theme revision and attention to divergent accounts. Participant consent and institutional approval are reported; no identifying transcripts are supplied.

## Findings — Theme example
The theme “success as renegotiated belonging” integrates participants describing identity changes, not simply job satisfaction. One participant described a higher-paid role as “feeling further from my people”; another described a lower-paid role as “finally work that sounds like me.” A contrasting account valued professional distance as independence. The full paper contains additional extracts, but they are not supplied here.

## Scope
These interpretations illuminate how these participants made sense of transitions in this context; they do not estimate prevalence or establish causal effects.
